title: Environment and Shared Dependencies
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of environment and shared dependencies in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply environment values in a small, inspectable example.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on environment and shared dependencies and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Environment values”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Application code connects state, UI, APIs, data storage and platform capabilities. Clear ownership and explicit failure states make the experience more reliable and accessible.

content_blocks.title: Module 17: SwiftUI State, Architecture, and Application Flow
content_blocks.alt_text: Module 17: SwiftUI State, Architecture, and Application Flow. Lessons in order: State Management Fundamentals; The @State Property Wrapper; Bindings with @Binding; Observable Application Models; Observation and View Updates; Environment and Shared Dependencies; Reusable SwiftUI Components; Conditional Views and View Composition; Navigation State and Deep Linking; Sheets and Full-Screen Presentations; Lists with Editable Data; MVVM and Other App Architecture Patterns; Managing Complex App State.
content_blocks.caption: Numbered overview of the SwiftUI State, Architecture, and Application Flow learning sequence.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** For environment values, separate app behavior from presentation and platform services. Define ownership and error states, test the behavior independently where possible, and verify Apple-platform requirements on a supported target.

**Work through the lesson.** Keep SwiftUI state ownership and data flow predictable while composing reusable screens and architecture. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

items.title: Environment values
items.text: For environment values, separate app behavior from presentation and platform services. Define ownership and error states, test the behavior independently where possible, and verify Apple-platform requirements on a supported target.

items.title: Environment objects and modern observable models
items.text: SwiftUI describes the interface as a hierarchy of views derived from state. Keep state ownership clear, compose reusable views, and verify keyboard, accessibility, and size-adaptation behavior.

items.title: Sharing dependencies across view hierarchies
items.text: ARC manages class-instance lifetimes through references. Strong cycles can keep instances alive; use `weak` or `unowned` only when the ownership/lifetime model justifies it.

items.title: Choosing between explicit parameters and environment injection
items.text: A function names a unit of behavior with typed inputs and a return type. Clear argument labels describe call-site intent and make APIs easier to read.

content_blocks.text: Use the compiler and versioned documentation as evidence. Do not treat a source-string check or an illustrative output as proof that a complete Swift program compiles on every platform.
